featured_reviews.name: Jon-Paul Lindsey
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Kalakar Tattoo and Art World recently and had a tattoo drawn by Akshaya. The majority of my tattoos are last minute ‘walk ins’, and I’ve had many from around the globe. Being ‘last minute’ the quality of the tattoos are usually sacrificed and it’s understandably difficult to fully connect with the tattooist as you only have a brief time to discuss, negotiate and agree etc. This was entirely the opposite case with Akshaya. From the moment I walked in, I felt extremely comfortable and within minutes we were discussing all the various options for the vague idea I had for my piece. Akshaya isn’t just a fantastic and patient listener; she’s a true artist in every sense of the word. I’m beyond elated with the finished work- she’s incredibly knowledgable, intuitive, caring and her soft touch with the gun is exceptional. The final piece is one of my most favourite and by far the very best I’ve had from a simple ‘walk in’. I cannot recommend her and her inherent skills more and can’t wait to get back to Goa so I can have and her genius mind do another piece for me. 10 stars, simply exceptional.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Rajaram Fine Art Insititute. it's one of pioneer  Institute for fine arts  in Mubmai (Ghatkopar and Matunga)which is training students from  last more than 70 years.and Legacy is still continued
Rajaram Fine Art Institute, provide quality art education to aspiring artists. Institute offers various courses in painting, sketching, for the needs of students with different levels of expertise.
And not just aspiring artist but for those children who join institute just as a hobby and then inspired to persue art as a career.

In 1979-80 one of my relative who was  ex-student  of Rajaram sir saw the flair of art in me and suggested  me to join  Matunga  branch.
Than I came in contact with Shrikishna sir, who  started his Branch at Ghatkopar & here I started  to learnt all the  mediums of art  & realistic  work. under  my Guru Shri krishna sir & this  helped me a lot in  my Art graduation at G D art  Drawing and Painting.
During my  art course in academic period of 1981 to 1986, at Raheja school of art time, I started assisting sir. ( morning hours & full time in vacation .)
After finishing my GD art painting course in 1986, I started assisting sir for full  time  till 1992.
In 1987 we started  Entrance  test courses for BFA & Architecture at Rajaram class.
This was the  turning point of my career.
During this time many students were joining class for hobby & than came to know that they can choose  art as a career & than they made susscsessful art career in different various fields.
An that's why  I always mention that,
"We design  your art career"
Now the 3rd  generation
(Rajaram sir, Srikrishna sir & now Shyam and Shreya.)
have  continuined   devloping the art skill  in  children of any age.
With the  sir's blessings  I am running my own  Institute from more than 35 years Under the banner "Vikrant Karia Institute of Art"  at Ghatkopar.
As an artist and an educator, I look forward to continuing the legacy of Rajaram Fine Art Institute and inspiring more and more individuals to pursue their passion for art.

I’m currently in my second year of BFA at NIFA (National Institute of Fine Arts), and the growth I’ve experienced here has been truly meaningful. In just over a year, my confidence, observation skills, and technical ability have improved in a way that reflects directly in my artworks.

Now, whenever I look at any subject or object, I feel equipped to translate it onto paper or canvas — something I couldn’t imagine before joining. This transformation has been possible because of the solid foundation and consistent mentorship provided at NIFA.

The classrooms are filled with beautiful and inspiring artworks, which constantly motivate us to aim higher. Being in such a creative space naturally builds discipline, focus, and artistic energy.

I’ve trained in multiple mediums here, including fine pen, acrylic, oil paints, watercolor, charcoal, and pencil shading. The guidance from Madhu Sir and Mandar Sir has been the most valuable part of my journey. Their experience, personal attention, and honest feedback have helped me grow both technically and creatively.

Alongside regular classes, NIFA also organizes enriching workshops like the Caricature Art Workshop, which allow us to explore different art styles and techniques beyond the syllabus.

You can view my art journey and progress on Instagram: @nishantchoudhary.arts — a reflection of everything I’ve learned here.

Even as I move forward in my art career, I will always remain a student of NIFA, and of Madhu Sir and Mandar Sir. I’m thankful to be part of this institute and highly recommend it to anyone serious about building their future in fine arts.
